title: Telemetry: canonicalize model/version identity in guardrails gating metrics (fix cross-region mismatch)
author: Caleb Johnson
body:
Problem: Guardrails gating metrics emitted by the control plane and ingested by the telemetry pipeline currently disagree on model identity in some regions. Specifically, us-east-1 emits (model_family, model_version) derived from the control-plane ModelRegistry, while eu-west-1 was emitting a runtime-resolved “served_model_id” (hash-ish) for certain Dedicated pools. This causes: (1) duplicate time series for the same model version, (2) dashboards showing apparent drops in pass rate after a rollout (really a key change), and (3) incorrect joins between OptimizeConfigChange audit events and gating summaries.

Root cause: The telemetry ingestion job had a region-specific fallback path that preferred ServingRuntime.model_id when control-plane version strings were missing. That fallback was triggered by an older field name (modelVersion vs model_version) still used by the EU control-plane deploy. The ingestion job then normalized metrics differently based on presence/absence of model_version, leading to cross-region divergence.

Fix: Introduce a single canonical model identity mapping step in the telemetry pipeline that produces a stable tuple used by all gating metrics and downstream joins: canonical_model_name (string), canonical_model_version (string), model_family (string), and source (control_plane|runtime_fallback). The mapping does the following: (1) prefer control-plane ModelRegistry identity when model_registry_id is present OR when model_name+model_version are present, (2) if only served_model_id exists, resolve via ModelIdentityResolver against the regional ModelRegistry cache (best-effort) and only then fall back to runtime id, and (3) enforce consistent key names + label set across regions.

Behavior changes: (a) gating metrics will stop emitting served_model_id as a primary label; it is retained only as a debug attribute in logs and as an optional high-cardinality tag behind sampling, (b) we emit a new label model_identity_source, and (c) we add a temporary compatibility mapping to translate the legacy eu-west-1 modelVersion field for 30 days.

Testing/validation: Added unit tests for identity canonicalization (including legacy field aliasing), added golden tests for metric label sets, and ran a backfill on staging metrics for 48h of traffic to verify time series collapse. Logan validated dashboard joins for pass_rate_by_model_version and override_rate_by_model_version.

Rollout: Safe to deploy independently. This is a telemetry-only change; it does not affect policy decisions. After merge, we’ll deploy to staging then prod (eu-west-1 first) and monitor: gating_metrics_dropped_samples, guardrails.metric_label_validation_failures, and dashboard series cardinality.

Notes: This also unblocks customer audit log requests where they want ‘proof’ the eval checks ran for a specific pinned model version (SUP-18544).
commits: ingest: normalize legacy modelVersion field and enforce label schema
metrics: add model_identity_source label; drop served_model_id from primary label set
tests: golden label-set tests + cross-region fixtures
docs: runbook note for interpreting model_identity_source and debugging mismatches
conversation: Jordan Lee (review): Can we guarantee this doesn’t change the gating decision payload? I only want telemetry keys to shift; policy/audit paths should remain untouched.

Caleb Johnson (author): Yep — this PR only touches telemetry ingest + metrics emission. The Optimize apply audit event still stores the raw model_version from control plane; we’re canonicalizing at ingest for metrics/dashboards only. Added a regression test to ensure we don’t mutate audit payload parsing.
Nadia Rahman (review): Please quantify cardinality impact. Dropping served_model_id as a label should help, but adding model_identity_source adds a dimension. Any risk of exploding series?

Caleb Johnson (author): model_identity_source is 2 values (control_plane|runtime_fallback). Net cardinality is down (we’re removing a high-card label). I added a golden test asserting label set and a dashboard note in the runbook.
Logan Wright (review): Good catch on the legacy modelVersion field. Can we time-bound the alias so we don’t carry it forever?

Caleb Johnson (author): Added TODO + config flag telemetry.guardrails.enableLegacyModelVersionAlias default-on with a 2025-04-01 removal date noted. Also emits a counter guardrails_legacy_modelVersion_seen so we can confirm it’s gone.
Sean Gallagher (review): For rollout, can we deploy eu-west-1 first since that’s where the bad path is? Also add an alert on label schema validation failures.

Caleb Johnson (author): Agreed. I added guardrails.metric_label_validation_failures as an alert candidate; actual alert wiring is in observability-pack but this gives the metric. Deployment order noted in PR body.
Felix Schneider (review): Does this fix the dashboard join with OptimizeConfigChange events (model_version mismatch)?
Caleb Johnson (author): Yes — gating metrics now emit canonical_model_version aligned with audit events. Verified in staging by joining on (tenant_id, route_id, canonical_model_version).
